memory_bridge: Stage three people around the two-legged figure: a Japanese person wears a 日本人 badge for On ジン, a headcount of three uses 三人 for On ニン, and one ordinary person alone answers to 人 for Kun ひと.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 日本人（にほんじん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Pin 日本人（にほんじん） to the standing figure like a nationality badge; its last character sounds On ジン and means “Japanese person.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 三人（さんにん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Now line up exactly three figures and let the counter call 三人（さんにん）; the counting reading is On ニン, “three people.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 人（ひと）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Leave one figure standing by itself and introduce that person simply as 人（ひと）; the native noun gives Kun ひと.
